add_company_scope:
Add domains/IPs/CIDRs/ICP filings/company keywords to a company's [asset scope] — domains, networks and ICP filings automatically claim matching assets; keywords are only given to the Agent as scope hints.
Company names are unique: if company doesn't exist it is created; if it exists it is reused (only the scope is merged in).
scope is one entry per line, recognized automatically: root domain / URL / single IP / CIDR range / ICP filing / company keyword.
Always give a reason explaining the basis for ownership (whois/certificate/ASN etc.).
Guardrails: bare TLDs and overly wide ranges are rejected (IPv4 prefix must be /16-/32, IPv6 prefix /32-/128); invalid lines are skipped and returned in errors.
add_hint:
Attach a strategic hint from the human/main agent to the exploration graph; the planner will read it the next time it generates intents.
★Prefer batching: put several hints into the hints array and submit them at once (saves round trips versus one call each). Returns an ids array, same length and order as hints (failed items have id=0, details in errors). For a single one, omit hints and give a top-level text directly.
add_intent:
Create [exploration directions], write them to the frontier and link them into the exploration chain. An intent is an open exploration direction, not a fixed type — describe freely in one summary sentence what to explore/verify/exploit.
★Prefer batching: put the several new directions picked in one round into the intents array and submit them at once (saves round trips versus one call each). Returns an ids array, same length and order as intents (failed items have id=0, details in errors). For a single one, omit intents and give a top-level summary directly.
add_task_hint:
Inject a strategic hint into the given task (its planner reads it when generating intents in the next round).
★Prefer batching: put multiple hints into the hints array in one submission (returns an ids array, same length and order as hints; failed items have id=0); for a single hint omit hints and give top-level text.
add_task_scope:
Add test scope to [this task] — this is the task's authorization boundary and also the denominator of asset test coverage.
Supported kinds: company (all assets under a company) / root_domain (a whole root domain, including all subdomains) / subdomain (a single exact subdomain) / ip / cidr / icp / keyword.
Note: hosts the worker touches one by one are added to the scope [automatically] by the system (exact subdomains); this tool is for [proactively widening] it — bringing in a whole root domain/company, or adding a specific subdomain/IP.
value: for company pass the company name or id (the company must already exist); for root_domain/subdomain pass the domain; for ip/cidr pass the IP or range; for icp/keyword pass the filing number or company keyword.
Always give a reason explaining the basis (auditable). Use the entries array for several.
bind_finding_traffic: Bind verified real HTTP traffic to an already recorded vulnerability. finding_id is the standalone vulnerability record ID; do not pass an exploration node ID. All references in a batch succeed or fail together; duplicate references do not overwrite existing notes. Binding marks any existing report as needing an update; do not re-probe or create duplicate vulnerabilities just to capture packets.
create_custom_tool: [IMPORTANT] After installing a tool the platform does not have, call this to register the installed tool in the platform so the platform can call it! Creates a custom tool (shell/command/script/http). shell = bash environment declaration; only key+description+agents are needed, no exec/schema.
create_mcp: Create an MCP server (stdio/http/sse). After creation its tools must be authorized per agent visibility.
create_skill: Create a new skill (writes SKILL.md, agentskills.io spec). name uses lowercase letters/digits/hyphens.
delete_assets_by_host:
Delete assets by exact host: removes the domain/subdomain for that host and the services (service) and endpoints (endpoint) under it.
host is an exact match (lowercased, trimmed), not fuzzy/wildcard.
Passing a root domain (e.g. example.com) also deletes its subdomains and their services/endpoints; passing a subdomain (e.g. a.example.com) or IP deletes only that host and its services/endpoints.
⚠️ Hard delete on the global asset store (shared across tasks); cannot be undone.
expand_digest: Expand a cold digest: returns a compact list of the members it folds (id/summary/state/confidence), the same shape as the overview's recent_facts/recent_done_intents. For a member's full details/evidence use node_detail(member_id).
get_finding_retest_context: Read the vulnerability evidence snapshot, retest status, extra notes and current task constraints linked to the current retest session. No parameters; can only read this session.
get_finding_traffic: Read the real traffic evidence bound to a vulnerability, independent of the capture toggle. finding_id is the standalone vulnerability record ID returned in the report_finding JSON (not the exploration node ID on the first line). First call without binding_id to get the list and version; an empty list is normal — for TCP or other non-HTTP vulnerabilities, or when nothing was captured, you can still write the report from text/command evidence, and binding is not required. When bindings exist, read the body in chunks by binding_id, side (request/response) and offset. When writing the report, pass the version you read as evidence_version to update_finding_report, whose finding_id is still the exploration node ID.
get_task_graph: Read the exploration graph overview of the given task (same as graph_overview: asset counts/frontier/findings/coverage, etc.); specify the task with task_id.
get_task_node_detail: Read the full content of an exploration graph node in the given task (finding/fact/intent/goal: summary + details/evidence/PoC). id is the exploration node id (e.g. returned by report_finding, or the id in list_task_findings). Use it to get a vulnerability's full evidence before writing its report.
get_task_worker_trace: View how a work (intent) in the given task ran: get_task_worker_trace(task_id, intent_id) shows step summaries; then pass step_ids=[...] to get the full content of those steps (at most 5 at a time; extras return only the first 5).
get_worker_output: Get the final output conclusion of an intent (work) in this task or a directly related task. Results from related tasks carry source_task_id/inherited=true and are read-only. A work that ended normally returns its summary; a terminated (stopped)/failed work returns its last output before the abort.
goal_met: [Immediately ends the whole task] — call it only when you have confirmed that [all of the task's goals have truly been achieved and the whole task is wrapped up] (note: this means the task is complete [as a whole]; achieving just one goal / one flag / one vuln [does not count] — in that case mark that goal with prove_goal). ⚠️It is not for "ending this planning round": when this round has no new intents to dispatch, or you are waiting for workers to produce output, [just end the round, do not call this tool] (0 intents is perfectly normal). For normal judgment prefer proving goals one by one with prove_goal; goal_met is only a way to bypass per-goal proof and wrap up globally.
graph_overview: (Exploration graph) Distilled summary of the exploration situation: asset counts, sites without endpoints, frontier, findings, hints (strategic hints from the human/main agent, which must be taken into account when generating intents). Call it first when planning.
insert_assets:
Register newly discovered assets in bulk; one call can mix several types (see the type enum).
Required fields per type: root_domain→domain; ip→ip (must be IPv4/IPv6, not a hostname); subdomain→domain; app→app_name; service (HTTP)→url; service (non-HTTP)→service_name+port (at least one of ip/domain); endpoint→url+method. See each field's description for the rest.
auth/technologies/params are appended and merged, not overwriting existing values.
Returns: {results:[{index,id,type}], errors:[{index,error}]}
kill_work: Terminate a running intent (work). Used to stop exploration that has drifted off course or is pointless; the terminated intent is marked stopped and is not automatically reclaimed. Check what it is doing with get_worker_output first before deciding.
list_assets:
Query the asset library: search by DSL expression, or fetch directly by id/ids; supports paging. Returns only assets within the test scope of [this task and its directly related tasks].
DSL: field=value fuzzy (ILIKE) | field==value exact | field!=value exclude | numeric fields support > >= < <= | bare word = full-text fuzzy; combine with AND/OR (AND binds tighter), parentheses for grouping. Asset type uses the separate type parameter, not the DSL.
When id/ids are not given, dsl must be non-empty (unconditional full queries are not allowed).
Available fields: domain (root/sub/service domain), root_domain, ip, url, page_title, icp, service_name, app_name, method (e.g. GET/POST), service_type (http|other), record_type (e.g. A/CNAME), technology (array, = fuzzy, == exact), port/status_code/company_id (integers).
Examples: status_code>=400 AND technology=shiro ; (port==80 OR port==443) AND technology=nginx
list_companies: List the [companies] in the asset library with their asset scope and number of attributed assets. Use it to see which companies exist and to get company_id (used when insert_assets associates an app, or list_assets filters by company_id). Optional search filters fuzzily by company name (case-insensitive); empty returns all.
list_facts: Page through the [exploration facts/conclusions] of this task and its directly related tasks, newest first (compact: id+summary+state; long summaries are truncated, use node_detail(id) for the full text). All parameters are optional: limit (default 20, max 100), before (cursor: pass the next_before returned by the previous page to get the next older page; omitted/0 = newest page), q (filter by summary keyword). Returns {facts, total, has_more, next_before}: total is the count after filtering; when has_more=true, continue paging with next_before. Entries from related tasks carry source_task_id/inherited=true and are read-only. For vulns see list_findings.
list_findings: List the [confirmed vulnerabilities] of this task and its directly related tasks (compact: id+task_id+intent_id+vulnclass+severity+summary+state). Entries from related tasks carry source_task_id/inherited=true and are read-only. Only vulns are included here; use list_facts for ordinary exploration facts and node_detail(id) for details.
list_goals: List this task's goal nodes and their states (open/met), to judge whether they have been achieved.
list_llm_profiles: List available LLM profiles: id, name, model, format, and whether it is the currently active profile. Use the id as spawn_task's llm_profile_id to give a subtask its own LLM (e.g. a cheap model for recon, a strong model for exploitation). Does not include the API Key.
list_task_findings: Read the confirmed vulnerabilities of the given task (including flag/PoC; each with id/task_id/intent_id/vulnclass/severity/summary/status); specify the task with task_id.
list_task_worker_traces: List which works (intents) ran in the given task + their step counts, to find works worth inspecting (then use get_task_worker_trace).
list_tasks: List all tasks (id/description/goal/status/runtime/parent task/LLM profile). The orchestration agent uses it to keep the global picture, see which tasks are stuck too long and which LLM each uses. Runtime: running = created → now, terminal = created → last activity (seconds). llm_profile: the profile name used by the task's planner/worker; (active profile) = follows the global active profile.
list_untested_assets:
Query assets in the scope of [this task and its directly related tasks] that are not yet covered by a fact anchor (related scope is read-only; for you to judge whether extra testing is needed, not a substitute for your decision).
Optionally filter by asset type: root_domain/subdomain/service/app/endpoint/ip.
Paging: page starts at 1, page_size defaults to 10. Returns {assets:[{id,type,label}], total, page, page_size}. Task context only.
node_detail: Get the full content of an [exploration graph node] of this task or a directly related task by id. Inherited nodes carry source_task_id/inherited=true and are read-only. Only for exploration node ids returned by list_facts/list_findings/graph_overview; for assets use list_assets/asset_neighbors.
pause_task: Pause the given task (stops its planner/worker loops).
prove_goal: Call this when you judge that a finding/fact proves a goal has been achieved: links the evidence node to the goal node and marks the goal met.
record_fact:
Write exploration [facts/conclusions] to the exploration graph, linked to the intent that produced them (intent_id). Used to record exploration results — including [positive conclusions] like fingerprints/enumeration, and [negative conclusions] like 'port closed' / 'parameter not injectable' / 'no login entry found'.
⚠️Multiple observations from one exploration must be [summarized into one fact], not split into several; whatever can be merged into one fact should be expressed as one fact as far as possible: summary = a one-sentence summary of this conclusion, detail = the related details (may contain several specific items). Example: fingerprint intent → one fact {summary:'Identified the tech stack and response characteristics of site X', detail:'nginx 1.25 / Vue3 / 200 / title=.. / body_len=..'}, rather than one fact each for status code, fingerprint and title. One intent usually produces only one fact; splitting too finely makes the graph grow without bound.
★The facts array is for writing several [mutually different] conclusions at once (each may omit intent_id, defaulting to the top-level intent_id). Returns an ids array, same length and order as facts.
⚠️Only write conclusions you [actually saw] in tool output; do not imagine them. evidence and confidence exist to keep inaccurate conclusions from polluting the graph:
  · evidence = [one line] of key evidence supporting this conclusion (command + the one or two most telling output lines), **keep it concise** — details already go in detail; don't paste large chunks of output here.
  · confidence = observed (seen directly in output) | inferred (inferred from symptoms).
  · **Negative conclusions** (not injectable / port closed / no entry found etc.) should only state "observation + tentative reading" — state what you actually saw; whether to abandon the direction is decided by the planner from the global picture. Always give evidence; if the methods weren't exhausted or the evidence is weak (including probing only once, or 'looks like'), mark inferred; mark observed only when truly exhausted and directly seen.
record_finding_retest_result: Save the single conclusion for the current retest session; the original vulnerability evidence and report stay unchanged. When the session ends successfully with the conclusion fixed, the system automatically sets the vulnerability status to fixed; other conclusions keep the original status. You must provide the evidence actually checked this time; when you cannot confirm, state the blocking reason.
report_finding: Record a confirmed vulnerability, using evidence to provide verifiable proof such as command output and logs. In a task context pass the current intent_id. The returned finding_id is the standalone vulnerability record ID and finding_node_id is the exploration node ID (the first line keeps that node number).
search_all_worker_traces: [Usually not recommended, since the system already provides most of the information] Search the [execution process of this task's other works] by keyword (q) — used to recover something a worker saw but didn't write into a fact (a path/token/error etc.). Steps of your own intent are excluded automatically (they are already in your context). Returns only summaries of matching steps (summary ≤100 chars), each with intent_id; then fetch the full content with get_worker_trace(intent_id, step_ids=[...]).
search_task_worker_traces: Search the execution of all works in the given task by keyword (returns matching step summaries + intent_id).
set_constraints:
Add operating constraints to [this task] to bound the exploration: type=allow (operations that are allowed) or deny (operations that are forbidden).
A constraint = a rule about "which operations may / may not be done" (e.g. "only test the current port, don't scan other ports", "no write operations against the production database", "passive recon only"); it is not a goal and not an attack step.
★Prefer batching: put several into the constraints array and submit them at once; the returned ids match it in length and order (failed items have id=0, details in errors). For a single one, omit constraints and give top-level text/type directly.
Only record constraints [explicitly written] in the task goal/description; do not invent them. When unsure of the type, use deny (more conservative).
set_goals:
Add exploration goals (goal) to [this task]. A goal = a final deliverable/verifiable result, not an attack step or recon action.
★Prefer batching: put several goals into the goals array and submit them at once; the returned ids match it in length and order (failed items have id=0, details in errors). For a single one, omit goals and give a top-level text directly.
vulnclass is optional: the corresponding vuln class (e.g. SQLi/IDOR); leave it empty for business-logic goals. Whether a goal is achieved is judged and marked met by the system; this tool only adds goals.
spawn_task: Create a new subtask and start its exploration engine; returns task_id. Use it to dispatch one thing (e.g. a challenge / a target) as an independent task. parent_ref is optional: set it to the parent task id associated with the current orchestration to link parent and child.
steer_work: Inject a live course-correction into a running intent (work) without interrupting it or losing its progress: the worker receives your instruction before its next action and adjusts accordingly. Use it for [within-intent] corrections like 'stop going down X, focus on Y'; if the whole direction is wrong, use kill_work and dispatch a new intent instead. Suggest checking what it is doing with get_worker_output first.
traffic_blob: Read the raw content of an oversized request/response body in chunks. Parts shown in traffic_get as '…[truncated] @blob sha256:<hash>' are stored here; pass that hash to get the full content. Returns at most 8KB per call; continue with offset (the result gives the total length). Suited to browsing backup files, source leaks, large JSON exports and other responses beyond the inline threshold.
traffic_get: Fetch the raw request/response of one captured exchange by id (truncated if too large). Use with traffic_search to avoid repeating curl.
traffic_search: Query target traffic already captured by the recording proxy (host is required; accepts a bare host, host:port or full URL, and can be further filtered by URL substring or body keyword). When a port is given, only that service's traffic is returned, so different ports on the same IP do not get mixed up. body_contains runs a full-text search over captured request/response headers and bodies, supporting any substring including CJK text (at least 3 characters). Returns only a very lightweight index (id/method/url/status/resp_len) without response content; when results are non-empty you must verify each request/response with traffic_get, then pass the IDs that genuinely support the current vulnerability to bind_finding_traffic. Returns 3 entries by default, at most 10 per page; use page to paginate when there are many results.
update_custom_tool: Update an existing custom tool (by key).
update_finding_report: Write/update the [detailed report] of a recorded vulnerability (full Markdown text, overwriting the old content entirely). finding_id is the id returned by report_finding (the number in "finding recorded: <id>"). A report should include: vulnerability overview, impact, reproduction steps, evidence/PoC, remediation advice.
update_mcp: Update an existing MCP server (by id).
update_skill_file: Write/overwrite one file inside a skill (default SKILL.md). Use it to change skill content or add scripts/references.
